newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Kohl, Patten thow protocol to the winds.
newsitem.headline: Kohl, Patten thow protocol to the winds.

text.p: Fortified by a 16 course trencherman's lunch and lashings of Tsingdao beer, visiting German Chanceller Helmut Kohl and Hong Kong Governor Chris Patten threw protocol to the winds on Friday and went shopping.
To the amazement of German tourists and passersby in the British colony, the pair dumped the official limousine, dropped in on Patten's favourite bakery and then hit Hong Kong's antiques row.
After a little help in haggling from the governor's assistant, John Tsang, Kohl emerged triumphant clutching a jade elephant.
Western Europe's longest serving leader also bought a jade turtle -- a symbol of longevity in Chinese mythology.
The pair then ducked into the incense-filled Man Mo temple and came face to face with a group of German tourists who quickly overcame their astonishment to reach for their cameras.
"It was a most unconventional official visit," Patten's spokesman Kerry McGlynn said.

Just like Patten's visit to Bonn last November, when 40 minutes of talks stretched on for 2-1/4 hours, their morning meeting ran on for double the alloted 50 minutes -- but neither let that encroach on lunch.
Giving the waiting media pack the slip, the two headed to a famous Chinese restaurant to feast on dim sum -- lunchtime dumplings -- roast goose, lobster, crab and assorted Hong Kong specialities.
Lunch was washed down with beer from the northeastern Chinese city of Tsingdao -- a former German colony where German expatriates founded the brewery that still exists.
Kohl arrived in Hong Kong on Friday on the third leg of a mission to strengthen Germany's ties with Asia-Pacific nations and expand business opportunities. He will depart on Saturday.
